record.final_answer:
No. I looked — there are no published numbers I can point to, and nothing in this repo either.

What's actually available to me: README.md and config/agent.yaml, one commit ("initial"), no benchmarks, no vendor docs offline, and no web search tool in this session (only direct page fetch, which needs a URL I don't have). So I can't confirm Marrowlog's docs publish TLS throughput figures, and I won't guess at one.

Two things worth flagging before you go looking for a number:

The unit in the question hides the real constraint. 50k lines/s at ~900 bytes is 45 MB/s ≈ 360 Mbit/s of TLS payload per agent, continuous, and agent.yaml reserves 1 vCPU per sidecar with batch_lines: 500 — so ~100 batches/s. A vendor's "lines per second" figure is usually for small synthetic lines with batching and a multi-core box; at your byte rate and core budget it says almost nothing. Bulk AES-GCM on one core is not the bottleneck (that's a few GB/s with AES-NI), so if something falls over it'll be per-record framing, syscalls/copies, and the fact that 360 Mbps is a serious sustained rate for one vCPU — not cipher math.

Nothing in the repo has been tuned for this. tls: false, buffer.disk: false. Enabling TLS then measuring is the only way to get a number that means anything for your shape of traffic.

Concretely, the cheapest path to a real answer: stand up a collector with TLS on and replay a captured peak-hour log sample through one agent on a 1-vCPU VM, one run plain and one TLS, and compare lines/s sustained and CPU saturation. That's an afternoon and gives you a defensible number for the security review instead of a vendor claim. If you'd rather ask Marrowlog first, the right question is "what's sustained TLS throughput and CPU per core for 900-byte records at 100 batches/s", not "how many lines per second".

Want me to write the replay harness and the config for the TLS run?
